title: Curses of the Fall: pain in childbirth, toil and thorns, return to dust
summary: God declared that the serpent would crawl, childbirth would be painful and the ground would yield thorns to hard labour. Johnson notes these came true literally from the expulsion from Eden onward.

title: Methuselah's name signals judgment at his death
summary: A common evangelical reading takes Methuselah's name as meaning roughly "when he dies, it will be sent". By Johnson's AM table (born 687 AM, lived 969 years) he died in 1656 AM, the year of the Flood.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Enoch foretells the Lord coming in judgment on the ungodly
summary: Enoch, taken by God in 987 AM per Johnson, warned of the Lord coming with myriads of holy ones to judge the ungodly. The Flood was a first judgment; Jude applies the prophecy to the final coming.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Lamech: Noah will bring relief from the cursed ground
summary: Lamech named his son Noah, saying he would bring comfort from the toil of the cursed ground. After the Flood God promised never again to curse the ground for man's sake, and Noah began farming the vine.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Noah and his family will be preserved in the ark
summary: God told Noah that the earth would be flooded but that he, his wife, sons and their wives would be kept alive in the ark with the animals. All eight came out alive about a year after the rain began.

title: In seven days it will rain forty days and nights
summary: God told Noah the rain would start in seven days and last forty days and nights. After seven days the fountains of the deep broke open and it rained for forty days.

title: Japheth will be enlarged
summary: Noah foretold that God would enlarge Japheth. At the dispersion his descendants spread across the coastlands and islands, becoming the widest-spread branch; many also see a later spiritual sense.

title: Abraham will die in peace at a good old age
summary: God assured Abram he would be buried in peace at a good old age. He died at 175, full of years, and was buried by Isaac and Ishmael.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates
summary: God defined the promised land as stretching from Egypt's river to the Euphrates. David extended Israel's rule to the Euphrates and Solomon held it; many hold a fuller fulfilment is still future.

title: Hagar will bear a son named Ishmael
summary: The angel told the runaway Hagar she would bear a son, to be named Ishmael, and that her seed would be countless. She bore Ishmael when Abram was 86.

title: Zoar will be spared and Lot escape there
summary: The angel agreed to spare the small town of Zoar for Lot and said nothing could be done until he reached it. Lot arrived as the sun rose, and the destruction fell on the other cities.

title: God will provide the lamb for the offering
summary: Climbing Moriah, Abraham told Isaac that God would provide the lamb. God stopped the sacrifice and supplied a ram caught in a thicket; Christians also see a later typological fulfilment. Year follows the tradition that Isaac was 37.

title: An angel will go ahead and a wife be found for Isaac
summary: Abraham assured his servant that God's angel would go before him to find Isaac a wife from his kin. Rebekah appeared at the well in answer to the servant's prayer and returned to marry Isaac when he was 40.

title: Two nations in Rebekah's womb; the elder will serve the younger
summary: God told Rebekah her twins would become two rival peoples and the older would serve the younger. Edom (Esau) was later subdued by Israel (Jacob) when David garrisoned Edom.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Isaac's blessing: peoples will bow to Jacob; he will rule his brothers
summary: Isaac blessed Jacob with abundance, rule over nations and lordship over his brother. Under David, Israel subdued the surrounding peoples including Edom.

title: Esau will live by the sword and serve his brother, then break free
summary: Isaac told Esau his line would live by the sword, serve Jacob's line, and later throw off the yoke. Edom served Israel from David's time and revolted under Jehoram (after this period).

title: At Bethel: God will keep Jacob and bring him back to the land
summary: In the ladder dream God promised to be with Jacob wherever he went and return him to Canaan. After twenty years in Haran Jacob came back safely to Shechem and Bethel.

title: A nation and kings will come from Jacob
summary: When renaming Jacob as Israel, God promised a nation, a company of nations, and kings from his loins. Israel's monarchy began with Saul and continued with David.

title: The cupbearer will be restored in three days
summary: In prison Joseph interpreted the cupbearer's dream: in three days he would be restored. On Pharaoh's birthday three days later he was returned to his post.

title: The baker will be executed in three days
summary: Joseph told the chief baker his dream meant execution within three days. On the third day Pharaoh had him hanged.

title: God will make Jacob a great nation in Egypt and bring it up again
summary: God promised to make Jacob's family a great nation in Egypt and surely bring it back. Seventy souls grew into a nation and left in the Exodus.

title: Ephraim, the younger, will be greater than Manasseh
summary: Jacob crossed his hands to give Joseph's younger son the greater blessing. Ephraim outnumbered Manasseh at the first census, produced Joshua, and became the leading northern tribe.

title: Reuben will not excel
summary: Jacob said unstable Reuben would lose pre-eminence for defiling his father's bed. Reuben lost the birthright to Joseph, settled outside Canaan east of the Jordan and produced no judge, king or prophet.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Simeon and Levi will be divided and scattered in Israel
summary: For their violence at Shechem Jacob said the two would be scattered. Simeon received towns inside Judah's territory and Levi received no territory, only 48 cities spread through the tribes.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Judah will be praised and his brothers will bow to him
summary: Jacob gave Judah the lion's place and the sceptre. The kingship came to Judah with David, crowned at Hebron and then over all Israel; the "Shiloh" line points on to the Messiah.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Zebulun will dwell toward the sea, bordering Sidon
summary: Jacob placed Zebulun by the sea toward Sidon. Its allotment lay toward the coast and trade routes between the Sea of Galilee and the Mediterranean.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Issachar will settle good land and bow to labour
summary: Jacob pictured Issachar as a strong donkey that sees the land is pleasant and accepts the burden. It received the fertile Jezreel valley, exposed to raids and forced tribute.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Dan will judge his people, like a serpent by the road
summary: Jacob said Dan would judge his people and strike like a viper. Samson the Danite judged Israel twenty years and struck the Philistines.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Gad will be raided but will raid back at last
summary: Jacob foretold that raiders would attack Gad but Gad would turn on them. Gilead east of the Jordan was oppressed by Ammon and then delivered under Jephthah; Gadite warriors later defeated the Hagrites.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Asher's land will yield rich food fit for kings
summary: Jacob promised Asher rich bread and royal delicacies. It received the fertile coastal plain of western Galilee, known for its olive oil.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Naphtali a hind let loose, giving goodly words
summary: Jacob likened Naphtali to a released deer with beautiful words. Barak of Naphtali led the swift victory over Sisera, celebrated in the Song of Deborah.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Joseph a fruitful bough, blessed above his brothers
summary: Jacob blessed Joseph with fruitfulness and the richest blessings. Ephraim and Manasseh became two large tribes with the biggest share of the land, including the central hill country.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: Benjamin will be a ravening wolf
summary: Jacob described Benjamin as a wolf that devours prey. The tribe proved fierce fighters, defeating all Israel twice at Gibeah, and produced Ehud and King Saul.

sources.name: Steady Ground: Did Jacob's final words to his sons come true?

title: God will visit Israel; carry Joseph's bones up from Egypt
summary: Dying at 110, Joseph said God would surely bring Israel to the promised land and made them swear to take his bones. Moses carried the bones out at the Exodus and they were buried at Shechem.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History (AM chronology table)

title: Sign to Moses: Israel will worship God on this mountain
summary: At the burning bush God gave Moses the sign that, after bringing Israel out, they would serve God at that same mountain. In the third month Israel camped at Sinai and met God there.

title: The elders of Israel will heed Moses
summary: Despite Moses' doubts God said the elders would listen. When Moses and Aaron showed the signs, the people believed and worshipped.

title: Pharaoh will refuse until compelled by a mighty hand
summary: God told Moses that Pharaoh would not let Israel go except under a strong hand. Pharaoh resisted through repeated plagues and released Israel only after the death of the firstborn.

title: Nile will be turned to blood
summary: Moses announced that striking the Nile would turn it to blood and kill the fish. It happened as he said and the Egyptians could not drink the water.

title: Frogs will cover Egypt
summary: Moses warned that frogs would swarm into houses, beds and ovens; they came up over the land, and died at the hour Moses set.

title: Swarms of flies, with Goshen spared
summary: Moses announced swarms "tomorrow" on Egypt but none in Goshen where Israel lived. The swarms came the next day and ruined the land, with the distinction kept.

title: Egypt's livestock will die tomorrow, Israel's spared
summary: Moses set the next day for a pestilence on Egypt's cattle, sparing Israel's. The Egyptian herds died and Pharaoh confirmed that not one Israelite animal was lost.

title: Unprecedented hail at this time tomorrow
summary: Moses announced the heaviest hail in Egypt's history for the following day. It fell with fire, destroying crops and exposed animals, but not in Goshen.

title: Locusts tomorrow will eat what the hail left
summary: Moses warned that locusts would cover the land and devour every remaining plant. An east wind brought them and nothing green was left.

title: Every firstborn in Egypt will die at midnight
summary: Moses announced that at midnight God would pass through Egypt and every firstborn would die, while Israel was untouched. It happened on the night of the Passover (Nisan 14-15), and Pharaoh released Israel.

title: The Egyptians you see today you will never see again
summary: At the sea Moses told Israel to stand still and see God fight for them. The sea parted for Israel and closed over the pursuing army; tradition puts this on the seventh day of Unleavened Bread.

title: Meat in the evening and bread from heaven in the morning
summary: On the 15th of the second month God promised meat at evening and bread each morning. Quail came that evening and manna appeared the next morning, continuing until Canaan.

title: Water will flow from the rock at Horeb
summary: At Rephidim God told Moses that striking the rock at Horeb would bring water for the people. Moses struck it and water came out.

title: Amalek's memory will be blotted out
summary: After the battle at Rephidim God vowed to wipe out Amalek, and Balaam said it would perish. Saul and David struck Amalek hard; the last remnant was destroyed in Hezekiah's day (after this period).

title: A whole month of meat until it comes out of their nostrils
summary: When Israel craved meat, God said they would eat it a full month until they loathed it, though Moses doubted it was possible. A wind brought vast quail, followed by a plague at Kibroth-hattaavah.

title: Only Caleb and Joshua of that generation will enter Canaan
summary: God exempted the two faithful spies from the sentence, promising Caleb the land he had walked on. Both entered, and at 85 Caleb received Hebron as promised.

title: The earth will open and swallow Korah's rebels
summary: Moses said that if the ground opened and swallowed the rebels it would prove God had sent him. As he finished speaking the earth split and swallowed them, and fire consumed the 250 men offering incense.

title: The chosen man's rod will blossom
summary: God said the rod of the man He chose would sprout, ending the dispute over priesthood. Next day Aaron's rod had budded, blossomed and borne almonds.

title: Aaron will die before entering Canaan
summary: After the waters of Meribah God said Aaron would be gathered to his people and not enter the land. He died on Mount Hor on the first day of the fifth month in the fortieth year.

title: Whoever looks at the bronze serpent will live
summary: During the plague of fiery serpents God promised that anyone bitten who looked at the bronze serpent would live. Those who looked recovered; Jesus later applied the image to Himself.

title: Balaam: Israel's king will be higher than Agag
summary: Balaam foretold that Israel would have a king exalted above Agag (the Amalekite royal title). Saul, Israel's first king, defeated the Amalekites and captured King Agag.

title: Balaam: a sceptre from Israel will crush Moab and possess Edom
summary: Balaam saw a star and sceptre rising from Israel to strike Moab and take Edom. David subdued both; the Qumran community and most Christians see the Messiah as the final fulfilment.

title: Moses will see the land but not enter it
summary: Because of Meribah God told Moses he would only view Canaan from a distance. Moses saw the land from Mount Nebo and died there at 120.

title: Joshua will lead Israel across and divide the land
summary: Moses commissioned Joshua, saying he would bring Israel into the land and give it to them as inheritance. Joshua led the crossing, the conquest and the division of the land.

title: The nations will dread Israel
summary: Moses said God would put fear of Israel on the peoples, and the Song of the Sea said Canaan's people would melt. Rahab told the spies that Jericho's heart had melted, and Canaan's kings lost courage at the Jordan crossing.

title: God will drive out the nations little by little
summary: God said He would not expel the Canaanites in one year but gradually, so the land would not become desolate. The conquest took a long time and much land was still to be taken when Joshua was old.

title: Israel will ask for a king like the nations
summary: Moses anticipated a day when Israel would say "let us set a king over us like the nations". The elders demanded exactly that of Samuel, and Saul was made king.

title: After Moses' death Israel will turn to other gods
summary: God told Moses that after his death the people would break the covenant and serve foreign gods, bringing disaster. After Joshua's generation died Israel served the Baals and was handed to plunderers.

title: Moses: Dan is a lion's whelp that leaps from Bashan
summary: Moses pictured Dan springing like a young lion from the north. The Danites, squeezed on the coast, struck Laish near Bashan by surprise and settled the far north.

title: Moses: Levi will teach Israel the law and serve at the altar
summary: Moses blessed Levi with the priestly duties of teaching statutes and offering incense. Levi received the priesthood and its towns throughout Israel rather than tribal land.

title: The Jordan will be cut off when the priests' feet touch it
summary: Joshua announced that when the ark-bearers stepped into the flooded Jordan the water would stand up in a heap. It did, and Israel crossed on dry ground on the 10th of the first month.

title: Ai will be delivered into Joshua's hand
summary: After Achan's sin was dealt with, God promised to give Ai to Israel through an ambush. When Joshua stretched out his javelin the ambush took the city.

title: Not one of the five Amorite kings will stand against Joshua
summary: When five kings attacked Gibeon, God told Joshua they would all fall to him. Israel routed them, with hailstones and the long day, and the kings were caught at Makkedah.

title: Tomorrow the northern coalition will lie slain
summary: Facing Jabin's huge northern alliance, God said that by the same time next day all would be slain and told Joshua to hamstring their horses. Israel struck them at the waters of Merom.

title: No one will be able to stand before Joshua
summary: God promised Joshua that no enemy would withstand him all his life. Scripture records that not one of Israel's enemies stood against them and God gave them rest.

title: The nations left in the land will become snares and thorns
summary: Moses and then the aged Joshua warned that Canaanites left in the land would become thorns and traps. In Judges Israel intermarried with them, served their gods and fell under oppression.

title: Judah will go up first and the land be given into his hand
summary: After Joshua's death the oracle named Judah to lead the attack and promised success. Judah defeated the Canaanites at Bezek and took Hebron and other cities.

title: Tomorrow Benjamin will be delivered into Israel's hand
summary: After two defeats at Gibeah, the oracle through Phinehas promised victory the next day. Israel ambushed Gibeah and Benjamin was nearly wiped out.

title: Deborah: Sisera will fall, and a woman will get the honour
summary: Deborah promised Barak victory over Sisera's chariots but said the glory would go to a woman. Sisera's army was destroyed at the Kishon and Jael killed him in her tent.

title: Gideon will strike Midian as one man
summary: God promised fearful Gideon he would defeat Midian, and that he would do it with just 300 men. The Midianite camp panicked at the trumpets and torches and was routed.

title: The Midianite's dream of a barley loaf: Gideon will win
summary: Gideon overheard an enemy soldier interpret a dream of a barley loaf flattening a tent as Gideon's victory. That same night Israel attacked and the camp fled.

title: Jotham's curse: fire between Abimelech and Shechem
summary: Jotham's fable warned that if Shechem had acted wrongly in making Abimelech king, fire would consume each of them. Abimelech burned Shechem's tower, then was killed at Thebez; the text says the curse came on them.

title: Manoah's barren wife will bear a Nazirite who begins Israel's rescue
summary: The angel told a barren woman she would bear a son devoted to God from birth who would begin to deliver Israel from the Philistines. Samson was born and fought the Philistines throughout his life.

title: Eli: God will grant Hannah's request
summary: Eli told the weeping Hannah that God would grant her petition for a son. She conceived and bore Samuel.

title: Samuel's first message: judgment on Eli's house
summary: God told the boy Samuel He would do something that would make ears tingle and fulfil all He had said against Eli. Israel was defeated, the ark taken, Eli's sons killed and Eli died on hearing it.

title: Eli's house will lose its priests before their time
summary: The man of God said no one in Eli's house would live to old age and his descendants would be cut down. Saul massacred the priests of Nob, Eli's descendants, with only Abiathar escaping; Solomon later removed Abiathar (after this period).

title: Samuel's three signs to Saul
summary: Samuel told Saul he would meet two men by Rachel's tomb, three men going to Bethel with bread, and a band of prophets, and would himself prophesy. All the signs came true that day.

title: Thunder and rain in the wheat harvest
summary: To show the people their sin in asking for a king, Samuel said he would call for thunder and rain during wheat harvest, the dry season. The storm came that day.

title: Saul's kingdom will not continue; a man after God's heart is chosen
summary: When Saul offered the sacrifice himself, Samuel said his dynasty would not last and God had sought another ruler. Saul's line ended and David became king.

title: Jonathan's sign: God has given the Philistine garrison into our hand
summary: Jonathan said that if the garrison told them to come up, it was God's sign of victory. They did, and Jonathan and his armour-bearer routed the outpost, setting off a Philistine panic.

title: David to Goliath: today the LORD will deliver you into my hand
summary: David declared that God would hand Goliath and the Philistines to Israel that day, without sword or spear. He felled Goliath with a stone and Israel routed the Philistines.

title: Keilah oracle: Saul will come and the town will hand David over
summary: David asked whether Saul would come and whether Keilah would betray him, and the answer to both was yes. Warned, David left with his men and Saul gave up the pursuit.

title: Pursue: you will overtake the raiders and recover everything
summary: After the Amalekites burned Ziklag and took the families, the oracle promised David he would overtake them and recover all. He struck the raiders and nothing was missing.

title: Go up: the Philistines will be given into your hand
summary: Twice in the Rephaim valley God promised David victory, the second time with the sign of marching in the treetops. David won at Baal-perazim and drove the Philistines back from Geba to Gezer.

title: Gad: three days of plague for David's census
summary: After David counted the fighting men, the prophet Gad offered him three punishments and David chose plague. A pestilence killed 70,000 until the angel was stopped at Araunah's threshing floor.

title: Jericho's rebuilder to lose his eldest and youngest sons
summary: Joshua cursed whoever rebuilt Jericho: he would lay its foundation at the cost of his firstborn and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest. More than 550 years later Hiel of Bethel did so and lost Abiram and Segub.

title: Micaiah: Israel scattered and Ahab will not return in peace
summary: Against 400 court prophets, Micaiah foresaw Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd and said Ahab would not come back safely. The army fled and Ahab died of a chance arrow.

title: Ditches filled with water and Moab defeated
summary: Elisha said the dry valley would fill with water without wind or rain, and Moab would be given into the kings' hands. Water came in the morning; the Moabites took it for blood, attacked, and were beaten.

title: Naaman will be clean if he washes seven times in the Jordan
summary: Elisha told the Syrian commander to wash seven times in the Jordan to be healed of leprosy. He did, and his skin became like a child's.

title: Gehazi struck with Naaman's leprosy for his greed
summary: Gehazi secretly took silver and clothes from Naaman. Elisha said Naaman's leprosy would cling to him and his descendants, and he left white with leprosy.

title: Moab's glory brought low within three years
fulfilment: Assyrian campaigns of Tiglath-pileser III (Moab made tributary)
summary: Isaiah said that within three years, counted like a hired worker's years, Moab's glory would be brought down. Johnson dates its capture by Assyria to about 732 BC.

title: Sennacherib will fall by the sword in his own land

fulfilled.label: 701 BC (Johnson's table, column alignment inferred; secular 681 BC)

summary: Isaiah said Sennacherib would hear a rumour, go home and be killed by the sword in his own land. While worshipping Nisroch, he was murdered by his sons Adrammelech and Sharezer.

title: Solomon promised unmatched wisdom plus riches and honour
summary: God promised Solomon wisdom beyond any king, along with riches and honour he had not asked for. Solomon became famous for both, exceeding all the kings of the earth.

title: Ten tribes to be torn from Solomon's son and given to Jeroboam

fulfilled.label: c. 964 BC (start of Jeroboam's reign, Johnson's date for 1 Kings 13)

summary: Ahijah tore his new cloak into twelve pieces and gave Jeroboam ten. After Solomon's death the ten northern tribes rejected Rehoboam and made Jeroboam king; Judah stayed with David's line.

title: Sign: the Bethel altar will split and pour out its ashes
summary: As a sign confirming his word against the altar, the man of God said it would split and its ashes spill. It happened immediately, in front of Jeroboam.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, 1 Kings 13

title: Jeroboam's son will die as his mother enters the city
summary: The blind Ahijah told Jeroboam's disguised wife that the sick boy would die as soon as she set foot in the city. As she crossed the threshold at Tirzah the child died.

title: Israel to be uprooted and scattered beyond the Euphrates
summary: Ahijah said God would root Israel out of the good land and scatter them beyond the River for Jeroboam's sins. Assyria deported the northern tribes to Mesopotamia and Media.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History, Basic Chronology (Shishak 2969 AM; Samaria 3205 AM; Jerusalem 3338 AM)

title: Judah given to Shishak but not destroyed
summary: Shemaiah said God had left Judah to Shishak, then, after the leaders humbled themselves, that they would not be destroyed but would serve him. Shishak plundered the Temple treasures but did not wipe Judah out.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History, Basic Chronology (Shishak 2969 AM; Samaria 3205 AM; Jerusalem 3338 AM)

title: Asa told he will have wars from now on
summary: Because Asa relied on Syria rather than God, Hanani said he would have wars from then on. There was war between Asa and Baasha all their days, and Asa ended his reign diseased and embittered.

title: Syria will return in spring and be defeated in the plain
summary: The prophet warned Ahab that Ben-Hadad would come back at the turn of the year, and said that because Syria called the LORD a god of the hills, Israel would win in the plain. At Aphek Israel killed 100,000 Syrians.

title: A lion will kill the man who refused the prophet's word
summary: A prophet told a man who refused to strike him at the LORD's word that a lion would kill him on leaving. A lion found him and killed him.

title: Jehoshaphat's ships with Ahaziah will be broken
summary: Eliezer told Jehoshaphat that because he partnered with wicked Ahaziah, God would break his ships. The fleet built at Ezion-geber was wrecked before it could sail to Tarshish.

title: Every male of Ahab's house to be cut off (after his days)
summary: Elijah declared Ahab's dynasty would be wiped out, but after Ahab humbled himself the disaster was put off to his son's days. Jehu killed Joram and all of Ahab's remaining house in Jezreel and Samaria.

title: Blood of Naboth repaid on Ahab's son in Naboth's field
summary: Jehu recalled the LORD's oath that Naboth's blood would be repaid in that very plot. He had Joram's body thrown onto Naboth's field.

title: The barren Shunammite will hold a son about this time next year
summary: Elisha told his childless hostess at Shunem that she would embrace a son at the same season the next year. She conceived and bore a son at the time he named.

title: A hundred men will eat twenty loaves and have some left

given.label: c. 878 BC (during the famine) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: During a famine Elisha said the LORD declared that a hundred men would eat twenty barley loaves and leave some. They ate and had food left over.

title: Siege of Samaria: fine flour for a shekel by tomorrow
summary: In a starving, besieged Samaria, Elisha said that by the same time next day flour and barley would sell cheaply at the gate. The Syrians fled in the night, and food sold at exactly the prices he named.

title: The doubting officer will see the plenty but not eat of it
summary: The king's officer scoffed at Elisha's word, and Elisha said he would see it but not eat of it. He was trampled to death in the gate by the crowd rushing to the food.

title: Hazael will do great evil to Israel
summary: Elisha wept as he told Hazael the harm he would do to Israel's strongholds and people. In Jehu's and Jehoahaz's days Hazael struck Israel's territory and left Jehoahaz only a tiny army.

title: Send away Israel's mercenaries and God will give victory over Edom
summary: A man of God told Amaziah not to take Israel's hired troops into battle, saying God could give him more than the money lost. He sent them home and defeated Edom in the Valley of Salt.

title: Jonah: Jeroboam II will restore Israel's borders
summary: Jonah son of Amittai had foretold that Israel's coast would be restored. Jeroboam II recovered the land from Hamath to the Dead Sea, and even Damascus and Hamath.

title: Amos: the sword will rise against the house of Jeroboam

given.label: c. 775 BC (under Jeroboam II, before Johnson's 770 BC for #66) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Amos said God would rise against Jeroboam's house with the sword. Jeroboam II's son Zechariah was publicly assassinated by Shallum after six months. (Standard dating puts Amos c. 760 BC and the murder c. 753 BC.)

title: The people of Syria will go captive to Kir
summary: Amos said fire would fall on Hazael's house and the people of Syria would go into exile to Kir. Tiglath-pileser III took Damascus, killed Rezin and deported its people to Kir.

title: Fire on Gaza; Ashdod and Ashkelon cut off
summary: Amos said fire would devour Gaza's walls and the rulers of Ashdod and Ashkelon would be cut off. Assyria took Gaza (734 BC) and Ashdod (711 BC); Babylon finished Ashkelon in 604 BC.

title: Israel will go into exile beyond Damascus
summary: Amos warned the northern kingdom that it would be carried captive beyond Damascus and Israel would leave its land. Assyria took Samaria and deported Israel to Assyria and Media.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Post-Flood History, Basic Chronology (Shishak 2969 AM; Samaria 3205 AM; Jerusalem 3338 AM)

title: Bethel's calf carried to Assyria; Assyria will be Israel's king
summary: Hosea said Samaria's calf idol would be carried to Assyria as tribute and Assyria would rule Israel. Shalmaneser made Hoshea a vassal, then took Samaria and its people.

title: Judah will be saved by the LORD, not by bow or battle
summary: While Israel would be shown no mercy, Hosea said God would save Judah himself, without weapons or horsemen. Jerusalem was delivered from Assyria by the angel of the LORD, not by battle.

title: The plot of Rezin and Pekah will not stand
summary: Isaiah told Ahaz not to fear Syria and Israel: their plan to install a puppet in Jerusalem would fail, and Assyria would plunder Damascus and Samaria. In 732 BC Damascus fell and Rezin and Pekah were dead.

title: Within 65 years Ephraim will be broken as a people
summary: Isaiah said Ephraim would cease to be a people within 65 years. After the deportations, Assyrian kings down to Esarhaddon settled foreigners in Samaria, ending Israel's identity there.

title: Samaria will become a heap, its stones poured into the valley
summary: Micah said Samaria would be a heap in the field and a place for planting vineyards, its stones poured into the valley. Assyria destroyed it; Stoner notes the hilltop is now gardens with its foundation stones rolled down the slope.

title: Assyria will flood Judah up to the neck
summary: Isaiah pictured the king of Assyria as the Euphrates in flood, sweeping through Judah up to the neck. Sennacherib took all of Judah's fortified cities but not Jerusalem, the head.

title: Egyptians and Cushites will be led captive by Assyria
fulfilment: Assyrian annals (Esarhaddon 671 BC; Ashurbanipal at Thebes 663 BC)
summary: Isaiah walked stripped for three years as a sign that Assyria would lead Egyptian and Cushite captives away naked. Esarhaddon took Memphis in 671 BC and Ashurbanipal sacked Thebes in 663 BC.

title: Assyria will be broken on God's mountains, by no human sword
summary: God swore he would break the Assyrian in his own land and that Assyria would fall by a sword not of man. The Assyrian army perished outside Jerusalem by the angel of the LORD.

title: Sign: eat what grows wild two years, sow in the third
summary: As a sign of deliverance, Isaiah said Judah would live off self-sown grain that year and the next, and plant and harvest normally in the third. The Assyrians left and farming resumed.

title: Sign: the shadow will go back ten steps
summary: Hezekiah asked for a sign of his healing, and Isaiah offered to move the shadow on Ahaz's stairway. The shadow went back ten steps.

title: Hezekiah's treasures and descendants will go to Babylon
summary: When Hezekiah showed Babylon's envoys his treasures, at a time when Assyria not Babylon was the power, Isaiah said everything would go to Babylon and some of his descendants would serve in its palace. Daniel and other royal youths were taken, and the treasures followed.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings only (612 BC Assyria; 607 BC Babylon; 537 BC Cyrus; 587-326 BC Tyre) - item text past #78 not readable

title: Zion will go to Babylon and be rescued there

fulfilled.label: 536 BC (Johnson: Cyrus' decree; his 2008 book heading reads 537 BC)

summary: In Assyria's heyday, Micah said the daughter of Zion would go out of the city to Babylon and there be redeemed. Judah went captive to Babylon and was freed by Cyrus' decree.

title: Jerusalem will be wiped as a dish and turned upside down
summary: Because of Manasseh, the prophets said God would stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria and wipe it clean. Babylon destroyed the city, and Kings attributes the end to Manasseh's sins.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, AM anchors (dsscalendar.org Onah intro: Temple 2935 AM, destroyed 3338 AM)

title: Huldah: disaster on Judah, but Josiah will not see it

fulfilled.label: c. 610 BC (Josiah's death; secular 609 BC) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Huldah confirmed the curses of the Law would fall on Jerusalem, but said tender-hearted Josiah would be gathered to his grave first. He died at Megiddo before the Babylonian invasions began.

title: The Judean prophet's bones will lie beside the Bethel prophet's
summary: The old prophet asked to be buried next to the man of God, saying his word against Bethel would surely come true. When Josiah burned the bones from the tombs, he left both prophets' bones untouched.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, 1 Kings 13

title: Shallum (Jehoahaz) will never return; he dies in exile
summary: Jeremiah told the people to weep for the king taken away, not the dead one, because he would never see his land again. Pharaoh Necho took Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died.

title: Egypt will stumble and fall by the Euphrates
summary: Jeremiah described Pharaoh Necho's army routed beside the Euphrates. Nebuchadnezzar crushed Egypt at Carchemish, and Egypt's king never again came out of his land.

title: Judah and the nations will serve Babylon seventy years
summary: Jeremiah said the land would be a desolation and these nations would serve the king of Babylon seventy years. Johnson's book runs Babylon's empire from 607 BC to Cyrus in 537 BC, seventy years.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings only (612 BC Assyria; 607 BC Babylon; 537 BC Cyrus; 587-326 BC Tyre) - item text past #78 not readable

title: Jehoiakim will have a donkey's burial and no heir on the throne
summary: Jeremiah said no one would mourn Jehoiakim; he would be dragged and thrown out beyond the gates, and none of his sons would sit securely on David's throne. His son Jehoiachin reigned only three months before Babylon took him.

title: Nebuchadnezzar will strike Kedar and the kingdoms of Hazor

fulfilled.label: 599 BC (Babylonian Chronicle: raid on the Arabs)

summary: Jeremiah named Nebuchadnezzar as the one who would plunder the tent-dwelling Arabs of Kedar and Hazor. In his sixth year the Babylonian Chronicle records him raiding the Arabs of the desert and taking their flocks and gods.

title: Coniah (Jehoiachin) taken to Babylon; no descendant to rule

fulfilled.label: 598 BC (Johnson-chronology 1st year of the captivity; secular 597 BC)

summary: Jeremiah said Coniah and his mother would be thrown into a foreign land, and none of his offspring would sit on David's throne. He was exiled to Babylon, and no descendant of his ruled Judah as king.

title: False prophet Hananiah will die within the year
summary: After Hananiah broke Jeremiah's wooden yoke and promised a quick return from exile, Jeremiah said God would remove him that year. He died two months later.

title: The nations will serve Nebuchadnezzar, his son and grandson
summary: Jeremiah said the nations would serve Nebuchadnezzar, his son and his son's son until his own land's time came. Evil-Merodach succeeded him, and Babylon fell under Belshazzar, a later descendant, in 539 BC.

title: Zedekiah will be brought to Babylon yet not see it

given.label: c. 593 BC (6th year of the captivity) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Ezekiel acted out the prince slipping out through the wall at night and said he would be brought to Babylon yet not see it, and die there. Zedekiah fled by night, was caught, blinded and taken to Babylon, where he died.

title: The crown removed until he comes whose right it is
summary: Ezekiel told Zedekiah to take off the crown: it would be overturned and no more until the rightful one comes. No Davidic king reigned in Jerusalem after 587 BC; the promised heir is read as the Messiah.

title: Babylon's king at the fork: divination will pick Jerusalem
summary: Ezekiel described Nebuchadnezzar at a fork between Rabbah and Jerusalem, consulting arrows and livers, and the lot falling on Jerusalem. Babylon came against Jerusalem and besieged it.

title: Ezekiel told the day the siege of Jerusalem began

given.label: 589 BC (9th year, 10th month, 10th day) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: In Babylonia, Ezekiel was told to write down the date because the king of Babylon had laid siege to Jerusalem that very day. Kings records the siege beginning on that exact day (secular reckoning: January 588 BC).

title: Pharaoh's arm is broken; he cannot rescue Jerusalem
summary: Ezekiel said God had broken Pharaoh's arm and it would not be bound up to hold a sword. Pharaoh Hophra's relief army drew the Babylonians off briefly, then went home without saving the city.

title: The Egyptian army will go home and the Chaldeans return
summary: When the Babylonians lifted the siege to meet Egypt, Jeremiah said Pharaoh's army would go home and the Chaldeans would return, take the city and burn it. They did.

title: Zedekiah will see Babylon's king eye to eye
summary: Jeremiah said Zedekiah would not escape, would face the king of Babylon in person, and be taken to Babylon. He was captured and brought before Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah. Ezekiel's word that he would not see Babylon also held, as he was blinded.

title: Jerusalem will be given to Babylon and burned
summary: Jeremiah repeatedly warned that Jerusalem would fall to the king of Babylon, who would burn it. Nebuzaradan burned the Temple, the palace and every great house and broke down the walls.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, AM anchors (dsscalendar.org Onah intro: Temple 2935 AM, destroyed 3338 AM)

title: Solomon warned: the Temple will be cast off if Israel turns away

given.label: c. 976 BC (13 years after his 989 BC Temple date) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: In a second vision God told Solomon that if Israel served other gods he would cast off the Temple and passers-by would be astonished. Babylon burned it, and Lamentations records the passers-by hissing.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, AM anchors (dsscalendar.org Onah intro: Temple 2935 AM, destroyed 3338 AM)

title: The Temple will become like Shiloh

given.label: c. 609 BC (start of Jehoiakim's reign) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: In his Temple sermon Jeremiah warned that trusting in the building was useless; God would do to it what he did to Shiloh. Within about twenty years it was burned.

title: Israel and its king to be taken to a nation they never knew
summary: Moses warned that disobedience would end with the people and their appointed king taken to an unknown nation. Jehoiachin and then Zedekiah were carried to Babylon.

title: Siege famine so severe that parents eat their children
summary: Moses warned that siege by a foreign nation would drive parents to eat their children. It happened in the siege of Samaria under Joram and again in Babylon's siege of Jerusalem.

title: Cities wasted, sanctuaries desolate, people scattered among nations
summary: The Law warned that rebellion would leave Israel's cities in ruins, its sanctuaries desolate and the people scattered. The Babylonian destruction was a first fulfilment; Stoner also points to the later Roman dispersion.

title: Ebed-melech will be spared when the city falls
summary: Jeremiah promised the Cushite official who rescued him from the cistern that he would not fall by the sword when Jerusalem was taken. Scripture records the promise but not his later life, so the fulfilment is implied.

title: Ezekiel will speak again when a survivor brings news

fulfilled.label: c. 586 BC (12th year, 10th month) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Ezekiel was told that on the day a survivor arrived with news of the city's fall, his mouth would be opened. The evening before the fugitive came, God opened his mouth, and the man reported that the city had fallen.

title: Philistia will be overrun by waters from the north
summary: Zephaniah said Gaza would be forsaken and Ashkelon desolate, and Jeremiah saw an overflowing flood from the north sweeping Philistia. Nebuchadnezzar sacked Ashkelon in 604 BC and the Philistines faded from history.

title: Moab will be destroyed as a nation
summary: The prophets said Moab would be destroyed from being a people and given to the people of the east. Josephus records Nebuchadnezzar subduing Moab and Ammon in his 23rd year; Moab disappears afterward.

title: Ammon's Rabbah laid waste and its people taken captive
summary: Amos, Jeremiah and Ezekiel said Rabbah of the Ammonites would become a desolate heap and its king go into captivity, the land given to the men of the east. Babylon subdued Ammon around 582 BC.

title: Edom brought down from its rock heights by its allies
summary: Obadiah said proud Edom, nested in the rocks, would be brought down and betrayed by its allies. Nabonidus campaigned through Edom about 552 BC, and Arab peoples drove the Edomites from Petra; by Malachi's day Edom's land lay waste.

title: Nebuchadnezzar will besiege and break mainland Tyre

given.label: c. 588 BC (11th year of the captivity) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Ezekiel named Nebuchadnezzar as the one who would besiege Tyre with siege works and tear down its towers. He besieged the city for about 13 years and took the mainland; the island fell later to Alexander (332 BC).

title: Egypt given to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for Tyre

given.label: 572 BC (27th year of the captivity) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Because the long siege of Tyre gave his army no plunder, Ezekiel said God would give Nebuchadnezzar Egypt as pay. A Babylonian fragment records his campaign against Egypt in his 37th year.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible C2000, Ezekiel 26 (13-year siege of Tyre by Nebuchadnezzar; Alexander later)

title: Nebuchadnezzar will set his throne in Egypt; the Jews who fled will perish
summary: In Tahpanhes Jeremiah buried stones where Nebuchadnezzar would spread his canopy and said the Jews who fled to Egypt would die there, except a few. Nebuchadnezzar invaded Egypt about 568 BC.

title: Pharaoh Hophra will be handed over to those who seek his life

fulfilled.label: c. 570 BC (Amasis overthrows Apries; killed c. 567 BC)

summary: As a sign to the Jews in Egypt, Jeremiah said Pharaoh Hophra would be given to his enemies as Zedekiah had been. Hophra (Apries) was overthrown by his general Amasis and later killed.

title: Nineveh will make an utter end; affliction will not rise twice
summary: Nahum said Nineveh's wound was incurable and its name would not continue. After 612 BC the Assyrian remnant fell at Harran (609 BC) and the city was never rebuilt; its site was lost for centuries.

title: Nineveh will be desolate and dry, a lair for beasts
summary: In Josiah's day, while Assyria was still a power, Zephaniah said God would make Nineveh a desolation where flocks lie down. It was destroyed in 612 BC and left as mounds.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings only (612 BC Assyria; 607 BC Babylon; 537 BC Cyrus; 587-326 BC Tyre) - item text past #78 not readable

title: An inferior kingdom (silver) will follow Babylon
summary: In Nebuchadnezzar's statue dream, the chest and arms of silver were a kingdom after his. Medo-Persia replaced Babylon in 539 BC. (Johnson's Daniel chart starts Persian rule over the Jews in 536 BC.)

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Daniel 11 Time Map (Persia 536-326 BC; Cambyses takes Egypt 525 BC; Xerxes I 486-465 BC)

title: Nebuchadnezzar will live like a beast for seven times
summary: Daniel read the dream of the felled tree: the king would be driven out to live like an animal until he acknowledged God's rule. Twelve months later, while boasting over Babylon, he lost his reason, and was restored after seven times.

title: The ram's higher horn comes up last: Persia overtakes Media
summary: The angel said the two-horned ram was the kings of Media and Persia, the higher horn rising last. Cyrus of Persia overthrew his Median overlord Astyages, and Persia became the dominant partner.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 8

title: The ram pushes west, north and south and none can stand
fulfilment: Persian conquests of Lydia, Babylon and Egypt
summary: The ram charged westward, northward and southward, and no beast could stand before it. Persia conquered Lydia and Babylon and, under Cambyses, Egypt, and campaigned against the Scythians.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 8

title: Elam and Media besiege: Babylon is fallen
summary: Isaiah saw Elam (Persia) and Media besiege the city while its rulers feasted, then heard 'Babylon is fallen'. Cyrus of Anshan in Elam, with the Medes, took Babylon during a festival.

sources.name: Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)

title: Babylon, the lady of kingdoms, will fall suddenly in one day
summary: Isaiah said the proud 'lady of kingdoms' would lose everything in a moment, in one day, despite her sorcerers. Babylon was taken almost without a fight in a single night.

sources.name: Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)

title: Babylon's waters will be dried up
summary: Jeremiah said a drought would come on Babylon's waters and God would dry up her sea. Herodotus says Cyrus diverted the Euphrates and his troops entered along the lowered riverbed.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 5 (gates; Isaiah 44:28-45:7; Jeremiah 51:57-58)
