title: Babylon's rulers made drunk at a feast and never wake
summary: Jeremiah said God would make Babylon's princes and wise men drunk at their feasts so they would sleep forever. Belshazzar was killed the night of his drinking feast.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 5 (gates; Isaiah 44:28-45:7; Jeremiah 51:57-58)

title: Babylon's warriors stop fighting; runners tell the king the city is taken
summary: Jeremiah said Babylon's soldiers would give up fighting and stay in their strongholds while runner after runner told the king the city was taken at one end. The Chronicle records the city taken without battle, and Herodotus says the centre did not know the outskirts had fallen.

sources.name: Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)

title: After seventy years, Babylon itself will be punished
summary: Jeremiah said that when the seventy years were complete God would punish the king of Babylon and his nation. Babylon's empire fell to the Medes and Persians.

sources.name: Fall of Babylon (Wikipedia; Nabonidus Chronicle, 16 Tashritu = 12 Oct 539 BC)

title: A conqueror called from the east and north to trample rulers
fulfilment: Cyrus' conquests of Media (550) and Lydia (547 BC)
summary: Isaiah described a ruler raised up from the east, a 'ravenous bird', who would come from the north and tread down rulers like clay. Chuck Smith reads these chapters as Cyrus, predicted about 150 years before his birth.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible C2000, Isaiah 41 (Cyrus named c. 150 years ahead)

title: Cyrus will be given hidden treasures of darkness
summary: Isaiah said God would give Cyrus treasures hidden in secret places. Cyrus took the fabled wealth of Croesus at Sardis and later Babylon's riches.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible C2000, Isaiah 41 (Cyrus named c. 150 years ahead)

title: Cyrus will free the exiles without price or reward
summary: Isaiah said Cyrus would build God's city and let the exiles go, not for payment. Cyrus freed the Jews, funded the work and returned the Temple vessels.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings only (612 BC Assyria; 607 BC Babylon; 537 BC Cyrus; 587-326 BC Tyre) - item text past #78 not readable

title: After seventy years for Babylon, God will bring the exiles back
summary: Jeremiah wrote to the exiles that when seventy years were completed for Babylon, God would bring them back. Ezra says Cyrus' decree came to fulfil the word spoken by Jeremiah.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings only (612 BC Assyria; 607 BC Babylon; 537 BC Cyrus; 587-326 BC Tyre) - item text past #78 not readable

title: The empty land will enjoy its sabbaths
summary: The Law warned that if Israel ignored the sabbath years, the land would get its rest while they lived in enemy lands. Chronicles says the land lay desolate seventy years to make up its sabbaths, fulfilling Jeremiah's word.

title: Fields will again be bought and sold in Judah
summary: With the city under siege, Jeremiah bought his cousin's field as a sign that houses and fields would again be bought in the land. The returning exiles resettled their towns and family lands.

title: Zerubbabel's hands founded the Temple and will finish it
summary: When the stalled work restarted, Zechariah promised that Zerubbabel, who laid the foundation, would also complete the house. Encouraged by Haggai and Zechariah, the builders finished the Temple in Darius' sixth year.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Daniel 11 Time Map (Persia 536-326 BC; Cambyses takes Egypt 525 BC; Xerxes I 486-465 BC)

title: A fourth, richest Persian king will stir all against Greece
summary: The angel told Daniel three more kings would rise in Persia, then a fourth far richer who would stir up everyone against Greece. Xerxes I, Johnson's Ahasuerus of Esther (486-465 BC), led a huge invasion of Greece in 480 BC.

sources.name: David Guzik (Calvary Chapel), Enduring Word, Daniel 11
Ken Johnson, Daniel 11 Time Map (Persia 536-326 BC; Cambyses takes Egypt 525 BC; Xerxes I 486-465 BC)

title: Mordecai: deliverance for the Jews will arise

fulfilled.label: 473 BC (13 Adar of Xerxes' 12th year) (Johnson chronology, derived)

summary: Facing Haman's decree, Mordecai told Esther that relief and deliverance would come for the Jews even if she kept silent. On 13 Adar the Jews defended themselves and were saved, and Purim was instituted.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Daniel 11 Time Map (Persia 536-326 BC; Cambyses takes Egypt 525 BC; Xerxes I 486-465 BC)

title: Zeresh: Haman will surely fall before Mordecai
summary: After Haman had to honour Mordecai publicly, his wife and advisers said that if Mordecai was a Jew, Haman would not prevail but would surely fall. That same day Haman was hanged on his own gallows.

title: Bronze kingdom (Greece) to rule over all the earth
summary: The image's bronze belly and thighs stand for a third empire after Babylon and Persia. Greece under Alexander took over the Persian realm. Johnson dates the end of Persia to 326 BC (secular: Gaugamela, 331 BC).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Iron kingdom (Rome) to break and crush all
fulfilment: History: Pompey annexes Syria and takes Jerusalem
summary: The iron legs stand for a fourth empire, strong as iron and crushing the others. Rome absorbed the Greek kingdoms, and Pompey took Jerusalem. Johnson dates Rome's period from 64 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Leopard with four wings: Greece's swift conquest
summary: The third beast, a winged leopard, pictures a kingdom that would conquer with great speed. Alexander took the whole Persian Empire in about a decade.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Leopard's four heads: Greek empire in four parts
summary: The leopard's four heads foretold a fourfold split of the Greek kingdom. After Alexander died it settled into four realms under Cassander, Lysimachus, Seleucus and Ptolemy.

title: Fourth beast, iron teeth: Rome devours the earth
fulfilment: History: Roman conquest of the East
summary: A terrifying fourth beast with iron teeth would crush all the earth. Rome took over the Greek kingdoms and Judea. The ten horns and little horn are still to come.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Goat from the west sweeps without touching ground
summary: A goat from the west comes so fast it seems not to touch the ground. Gabriel names it Greece (8:21). Alexander's army moved from Macedonia into Asia at astonishing speed.

title: Goat breaks the ram's two horns (Greece defeats Medo-Persia)
summary: The goat attacks the two-horned ram, named as Media and Persia, and tramples it. Alexander defeated Darius III in three battles and ended the Persian Empire. Johnson dates this to 326 BC; secular dating has 331 BC.

title: Great horn broken at the height of its strength
summary: When the goat was strongest its great horn would be broken. Alexander died suddenly in Babylon, at the peak of his power, aged about 32 (traditionally 10 or 11 June 323 BC).

title: Four horns toward the four winds replace the great horn
summary: Four notable horns would rise in place of the broken horn, but without its power. Alexander's generals divided his realm into four kingdoms, none as strong as his.

title: Tyre's wealth cast into the sea and the city burned
fulfilment: History: Alexander's seven-month siege of Tyre
summary: Tyre had walled itself in and piled up silver and gold, but the Lord would strike her power in the sea and burn her. Alexander besieged island Tyre for seven months and destroyed it.

title: God will encamp about His house: Jerusalem spared
summary: God promised to guard His house against the army passing through. Alexander marched past Jerusalem without destroying it. Josephus says he honoured the high priest and was shown Daniel's prophecy about Greece.

title: Tyre's stones and timber laid in the midst of the water
fulfilment: History: Alexander's causeway to island Tyre
summary: Ezekiel foretold many nations against Tyre, her stones and dust thrown into the sea and the site left like bare rock. Alexander scraped the ruins of mainland Tyre into the sea to build a causeway to the island. Johnson's book frames Tyre's fall as 587-326 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Sons of Zion raised against the sons of Greece
summary: God would arm the sons of Zion against the sons of Greece (Javan). The Maccabees rose against the Greek Seleucid king Antiochus IV and won.

title: An altar to the LORD in the midst of Egypt
summary: Isaiah saw Egyptian cities speaking the language of Canaan and an altar to the LORD in Egypt. Onias IV built a Jewish temple at Leontopolis and, Josephus says, appealed to this passage. The worldwide turning of Egypt is still future.

title: Kingdom not passed to his descendants
fulfilment: History: murders of Alexander IV and Heracles
summary: The kingdom would not go to his posterity. Alexander's sons, Alexander IV and Heracles, were murdered, and the line ended.

title: Kingdom divided toward the four winds
summary: The empire would be divided to the four winds and ruled by others. Johnson names the four as Seleucus Nicator, Cassander, Lysimachus and Ptolemy.

title: King of the North invades the South and returns home
summary: The king of the North would come into the South's kingdom but go back to his own land. Seleucus II's counter-attack on Egypt failed.

title: King of the South defeats the great northern army
summary: The enraged southern king would fight the northern multitude and win. Ptolemy IV beat Antiochus III at Raphia in 217 BC.

title: The southern victor kills tens of thousands but does not prevail
summary: After casting down many thousands, the southern king would not press his advantage. Ptolemy IV made peace instead of conquering Syria. Johnson cites Polybius for over 10,000 dead.

title: North takes a well-fortified city
fulfilment: History: Battle of Panium; siege of Sidon
summary: The northern king would besiege and capture a fortified city, and the South's best troops could not stop him. Antiochus III won at Panium and forced Scopas to surrender at Sidon.

title: He stumbles and falls and is not found
fulfilment: History: death of Antiochus III at Elymais
summary: He would go back to his own fortresses, stumble and fall. Antiochus III was killed while plundering a temple of Bel in Elymais (Johnson: 187 BC).

title: Great army against the South; the South betrayed by his own
summary: He would march against the South with a great army, and the southern king would be undone by the counsel of those who ate at his table. Antiochus IV defeated Ptolemy VI, whose advisers had pushed him into the war.

title: Two kings speak lies at one table
fulfilment: History: Antiochus IV and Ptolemy VI at Memphis
summary: Both kings, bent on mischief, would lie to each other at one table. Antiochus held Ptolemy VI as a 'guest' while each plotted against the other.

title: He returns with riches, his heart against the holy covenant
summary: Coming home with great wealth, he would act against the holy covenant. Antiochus plundered the Temple in Jerusalem (Johnson: 169 BC, after deposing Jason).

title: Ships of Kittim come against him; he turns back grieved
summary: On a second invasion of the South it would not go as before: ships from Kittim would come against him. The Roman envoy Popillius Laenas drew a circle around Antiochus and made him leave Egypt.

title: Sanctuary profaned, daily sacrifice ended, abomination set up
summary: His forces would defile the sanctuary, stop the daily sacrifice and set up the abomination that makes desolate. Antiochus put a pagan altar on the Temple altar (secular: 15/25 Kislev 167 BC). Johnson's map heads this 165 BC and sees it as a type of the Antichrist.

title: Those who forsake the covenant corrupted by flatteries
summary: He would favour those who forsook the covenant and corrupt them with flattery. Hellenising Jews such as Jason and Menelaus took his side and abandoned the Law.

title: Little horn grows toward south, east and the Pleasant Land
fulfilment: History: Antiochus IV's campaigns in Egypt, Persia, Judea
summary: From one of the four horns a little horn would grow great toward the south, the east and the Pleasant Land. Antiochus IV campaigned in Egypt, in the east, and in Judea.

title: Daily sacrifice taken away and sanctuary cast down
summary: The horn would set itself against the Prince of the host, remove the daily sacrifice and throw down the sanctuary. Antiochus banned the sacrifices and defiled the Temple. Chuck Smith says he offered a pig on the altar.

title: After 2,300 evenings and mornings the sanctuary is cleansed
summary: Daniel heard that the sanctuary would be restored after 2,300 evenings and mornings. Judas Maccabeus cleansed and rededicated the Temple on 25 Kislev 164 BC, the origin of Hanukkah. Chuck Smith rejects reading the figure as 2,300 years.

title: A fierce king, mighty but not by his own power, destroys the holy people
summary: In the latter part of the four kingdoms a fierce, cunning king would rise and destroy many of the holy people. Antiochus' forces massacred Jerusalemites and enslaved others. Chuck Smith and Johnson also see a future Antichrist in him.

title: He will be broken without human hand
summary: This king would stand against the Prince of princes but be broken without human hand. Antiochus IV died of illness in Persia, not in battle (Johnson: 164 BC).

title: Ships from Kittim will afflict Asshur and Eber

given.label: c. 1437 BC (end of the wilderness years)

fulfilment: History: Rome annexes Syria and takes Jerusalem
summary: Balaam foresaw ships from Kittim afflicting Asshur and Eber. Johnson reads Kittim as Rome, Asshur as Syria and Eber as Israel: Pompey ended the Seleucid kingdom and took Jerusalem.

title: The promised line will come through Isaac
summary: The covenant line was to run through Isaac, not Ishmael. Luke's genealogy traces Jesus through Isaac.

title: Sceptre not to depart from Judah until Shiloh comes

fulfilled.label: c. AD 6-7 (Archelaus deposed; Roman direct rule)

fulfilment: History: Judea becomes a Roman province
summary: Judah's ruling authority would last until Shiloh came. Evangelical writers note Messiah was born before Judea lost its self-rule: Archelaus was deposed in AD 6 and Rome took direct control, including capital cases.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Lo, I come: to do Your will (body prepared)
summary: The psalmist says sacrifices did not satisfy God and one comes to do His will. Hebrews applies this to Christ's coming into the world.

title: David's son is David's Lord
summary: David calls the coming king 'my Lord'. The angels announced Jesus as Christ the Lord, and Jesus used the verse to show the Messiah was more than David's son.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: The glory of the latter house greater than the former
summary: Haggai promised the rebuilt Temple would have greater glory than Solomon's. Evangelicals see this in the Messiah himself entering the Second Temple, from his presentation as an infant onward.

title: Gabriel: Elizabeth will bear a son named John

given.label: c. 3 BC (in the course of Abijah)

fulfilled.label: c. Passover, 2 BC (Johnson: John born about Nisan 15)

summary: Gabriel told the elderly priest Zacharias that his barren wife would bear a son, to be named John. John was born and named as foretold. Johnson places his birth near Passover, about six months before Jesus.

title: Gabriel: Mary will conceive the Son of the Highest
summary: Gabriel told Mary she would conceive by the Holy Spirit and bear a son named Jesus, Son of the Most High. The child was born and named Jesus.

title: Shepherds will find the babe in a manger
summary: The angel gave the shepherds a sign: a newborn wrapped in cloths, lying in a manger. They went to Bethlehem and found him just so.

title: Simeon will not die before seeing the Lord's Christ
summary: The Spirit had promised Simeon he would see the Messiah before he died. He held the infant Jesus in the Temple and blessed God.

title: A sword will pierce Mary's soul; the child set for falling and rising
summary: Simeon said the child would be opposed and a sword would pierce his mother's soul. Mary stood at the cross and watched her son die.

title: Flee to Egypt, for Herod will seek the child
summary: An angel warned that Herod would seek to kill the child. Herod sent soldiers to kill the boys of Bethlehem, and the family returned only after he died.

title: Elijah the prophet sent before the day of the LORD
summary: God would send Elijah before the great day of the LORD. Jesus said John came in Elijah's spirit, and Johnson ties John to Elijah's cup at the Seder. Many also expect a future Elijah (Revelation 11).

title: Behold the Lamb of God (Passover lamb identified)
summary: John called Jesus the Lamb of God who takes away the world's sin. Johnson notes Jesus died at 3 PM on Nisan 14, when the Passover lambs were slain.

title: I will open my mouth in parables
summary: The psalmist would speak in parables and dark sayings from of old. Jesus taught the crowds in parables, which Matthew says fulfilled this.

title: He will not cry out, break a bruised reed, or quench smoking flax
summary: The Servant would be quiet and gentle with the weak. Jesus healed the crowds and told them not to make him known, as Matthew notes.

title: A light to the Gentiles, salvation to the ends of the earth

fulfilled.label: c. AD 47 (Paul and Barnabas turn to Gentiles)

summary: The Servant would be a light to the nations as well as Israel. The gospel went out to the Gentiles, and Paul quoted this when he turned to them. Its spread to the ends of the earth continues.

title: A stranger to my brothers, an alien to my mother's children
summary: The sufferer would be estranged from his own brothers. Jesus' brothers did not believe in him during his ministry.

title: Who has believed our report?
summary: Isaiah asks who would believe the message about the arm of the LORD. Despite many signs, most did not believe Jesus, which John says fulfilled Isaiah.

title: Some standing here will see the Son of Man in His kingdom
summary: Jesus said some present would not die before seeing him in kingdom glory. Six days later Peter, James and John saw him transfigured.

title: The first fish caught will have a coin for the tax
summary: Jesus told Peter that the first fish he caught would have a coin in its mouth to pay the Temple tax for both of them.

title: Lazarus' sickness is not to death; I go to wake him
summary: Jesus said Lazarus' illness would not end in death and that he would wake him. After four days in the tomb, Lazarus came out alive.

title: Caiaphas: one man should die for the nation
summary: The high priest said one man should die for the people, and John says he unknowingly prophesied Jesus' death for the nation and God's scattered children.

title: Street and wall rebuilt in troubled times (first seven weeks)

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: Jerusalem would be rebuilt with street and wall in troublous times during the first seven weeks. Nehemiah rebuilt the walls under opposition after the decree Johnson dates to Nisan 444 BC.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: Hosanna: blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD
summary: The festival psalm greets the one coming in the LORD's name. The crowds sang these words as Jesus entered Jerusalem.

title: Out of the mouths of babes You have perfected praise
summary: God draws praise from children and infants. Children in the Temple cried 'Hosanna to the Son of David', and Jesus quoted this psalm to the angry priests.

title: Passover lamb chosen on the 10th day and inspected
summary: The Passover lamb was chosen on Nisan 10 and kept until the 14th. Johnson notes Jesus presented himself in Jerusalem and the Temple on Nisan 10 and was examined and found without fault.

sources.name: Skip Heitzig, God's Precision (Connection devotional, Jan 2025)

title: You will find a colt tied, on which no man has sat
summary: Jesus sent two disciples to a village where they would find an unridden colt, and told them what the owners would say. It happened exactly so.

title: The kingdom will be taken from you and given to a nation bearing fruit
summary: In the parable of the tenants, Jesus warned the leaders that the vineyard would be taken from them and they would be destroyed. The gospel went to the Gentiles and the Temple leadership fell in AD 70.

title: Anointed beforehand for burial
summary: Jesus said Mary's anointing at Bethany prepared his body for burial. Within a week he was dead and buried.

title: Delivered to the Gentiles to be mocked, scourged and crucified
summary: On the road to Jerusalem Jesus said the chief priests would condemn him and hand him to the Gentiles to be mocked, spat on, scourged and crucified. Every detail followed.

title: The Son of Man must be lifted up (death by crucifixion)
summary: Like Moses' bronze serpent, the Son of Man would be lifted up, which pointed to death by crucifixion. A Roman cross rather than Jewish stoning fulfilled it, as John notes.

title: They will strike the Judge of Israel with a rod on the cheek
summary: Micah saw the ruler of Israel struck on the cheek. Johnson says it was fulfilled in AD 32 when the Roman soldiers struck and mocked Jesus.

title: Let another take his office
summary: The psalm says another would take the betrayer's office. Peter cited it, and Matthias was chosen to replace Judas among the Twelve.

title: A man carrying a pitcher will show you a large upper room
summary: Jesus told two disciples to follow a man carrying a water jar to a house with a furnished upper room. They found everything as he said.

title: After I am raised I will go before you into Galilee
summary: Jesus promised to meet his scattered disciples in Galilee after his resurrection. He appeared to them on a mountain and by the Sea of Galilee.

title: His appearance marred more than any man
summary: The Servant would be disfigured beyond human likeness. Chuck Smith links this to the beatings Jesus took while blindfolded and to the crown of thorns.

title: He made intercession for the transgressors
summary: The Servant would pray for transgressors. On the cross Jesus prayed 'Father, forgive them'. Chuck Smith cites this.

title: The LORD laid on Him the iniquity of us all
summary: The Servant would be wounded for others' transgressions and made an offering for sin. The apostles teach that Jesus bore our sins in his body on the cross.

title: They gave Me gall for food and vinegar for My thirst
summary: His enemies would give him gall and sour wine. Jesus was offered wine mixed with gall, then vinegar on a sponge.

title: I will make the sun go down at noon
summary: God would darken the earth in broad daylight. Darkness covered the land from the sixth to the ninth hour while Jesus hung on the cross. Many also see a future day-of-the-LORD fulfilment.

title: He who is hanged on a tree is accursed

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: The Law cursed anyone hanged on a tree and required burial the same day. Paul says Christ became a curse for us on the tree, and the body was taken down before evening.

title: Feast of Unleavened Bread: the sinless one buried
summary: The Feast of Unleavened Bread began on Nisan 15. Johnson teaches that Jesus, sinless like unleavened bread, was buried as Nisan 15 began.

title: Daughters of Jerusalem, weep for yourselves and your children
summary: On the way to the cross Jesus told the mourning women to weep for themselves, because days would come when the barren would be called blessed. Jerusalem's siege brought famine and slaughter in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: You will not leave My soul in Sheol nor let Your Holy One see corruption
summary: David wrote that God's Holy One would not decay in the grave. Peter and Paul preached that David's tomb was still occupied but Jesus rose without decay.

title: First Fruits waved the day after the Sabbath
summary: The first sheaf of harvest was waved before God the day after the Sabbath. Johnson teaches that First Fruits fell on Sunday, Nisan 17, AD 32, the day Christ rose. On the DSS calendar it is 26 Nisan, the barley First Fruits.

title: I will declare Your name to My brethren
summary: Psalm 22 turns from suffering to the sufferer praising God among his brothers. On resurrection morning Jesus sent word to 'my brethren'.

title: Sit at My right hand until I make Your enemies Your footstool
summary: The LORD invites David's Lord to sit at His right hand. The apostles say Jesus is enthroned there now. Putting his enemies under his feet is still being completed.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict, messianic prophecy list (as summarised online)

title: Feast of Weeks: new offering fifty days after First Fruits
summary: Fifty days from First Fruits, Israel offered two leavened loaves of new grain. Johnson teaches the Spirit came on that day (Sivan 6, lunar reckoning) and 3,000 were saved, the birth of the Church. On the DSS calendar it is 15 Sivan.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), period headings (book text past c. 711 BC not readable; no item numbers)

title: Witnesses in Jerusalem, Judea, Samaria and the ends of the earth
summary: Jesus said the Spirit-empowered disciples would witness outward from Jerusalem. Acts traces the gospel from Jerusalem to Samaria and on to Rome. The spread to every nation continues.

title: You will be delivered to councils and scourged in synagogues
summary: Jesus warned that his messengers would be arrested, flogged and killed. The apostles were jailed and beaten by the Sanhedrin, and Stephen and James were killed.

title: James and John will drink of My cup
summary: Jesus told James and John they would share his suffering. James was beheaded by Herod Agrippa I (died AD 44), and John was exiled to Patmos.

title: Peter will stretch out his hands and be led where he would not go
summary: Jesus told Peter that when old he would stretch out his hands and be bound and led away, pointing to the death he would die. Early church tradition records Peter's crucifixion in Rome under Nero.

title: Paul will bear My name before Gentiles and kings and suffer much
summary: The Lord said Saul would carry His name to Gentiles, kings and Israel, and would suffer for it. Paul preached across the empire, stood before Felix, Festus and Agrippa, and endured much.

title: A great famine throughout the world
summary: The prophet Agabus foretold a great famine. Luke notes it came under Claudius, and Josephus describes severe famine in Judea at that time.

title: You must also bear witness at Rome
summary: The Lord told the imprisoned Paul he would testify in Rome. Paul reached Rome and preached there for two years.

title: Ship lost but no life lost; aground on an island
summary: In the storm Paul said the ship would be lost but all aboard saved after running aground on an island. All 276 reached the shore of Malta.

title: Many will come in My name saying 'I am Christ'
summary: Jesus warned of false messiahs and prophets. Josephus records Theudas and 'the Egyptian', and Simon bar Kokhba was hailed as Messiah in AD 132. Jesus said more would come before the end.

title: Its end with a flood; desolations determined

given.label: 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

fulfilment: History: Bar Kokhba war; Aelia Capitolina
summary: War and desolations would continue to the end like a flood. After AD 70 came the crushing of the Bar Kokhba revolt, when Hadrian expelled Jews from Jerusalem. Johnson dates the Roman dispersion to 4057 AM (AD 132).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Your house is left to you desolate
summary: Mourning over Jerusalem, Jesus said its house would be left desolate. Chuck Smith reads this as the end of Israel's season of grace, followed by the AD 70 destruction.

title: All these things shall come upon this generation
summary: Jesus said judgment for the blood of the righteous would fall on that very generation. Jerusalem fell about 38 years later, within a generation.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Enemies will hem Jerusalem in and level it with its children
summary: Weeping over the city at the entry, Jesus said enemies would wall it in, hem it in on every side and dash it and its children to the ground, because it did not know the time of its visitation. Titus built a siege wall around Jerusalem and destroyed it.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Then let those in Judea flee to the mountains
summary: Jesus told his followers to get out of Jerusalem as soon as the armies appeared. Eusebius records that the Jerusalem church, warned by a revelation, fled across the Jordan to Pella before the siege.

title: Great distress in the land and wrath on this people
summary: Jesus spoke of woe for nursing mothers and great distress in the land. Josephus describes the siege's famine and the deaths of over a million people. Matthew's wording also looks to the future Great Tribulation.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: The king sent his armies, destroyed those murderers and burned their city
summary: In the wedding feast parable the king, angered at the killing of his servants, sends armies to burn their city. Rome burned Jerusalem in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Led captive into all nations; Jerusalem trodden down by Gentiles
summary: Jesus said Jerusalem's people would die by the sword or be taken captive to every nation, and the city trodden down by Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles end. Josephus counts 97,000 captives in AD 70, and the dispersion followed in AD 132 (Johnson). Gentile rule over Jerusalem lasted into modern times.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews
Ken Johnson, dsscalendar.org Enoch weeks (week 6: AD 32, AD 70, AD 132)

title: Open your doors, O Lebanon, that fire may devour your cedars
summary: Zechariah calls on 'Lebanon' to open its doors to fire. The Talmud says the Temple doors opened by themselves forty years before the destruction and Yohanan ben Zakkai linked this verse to the Temple burning. The cedar-lined Temple burned in AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: A nation from afar, swift as the eagle, of a language you do not understand

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: Moses warned of a fierce foreign nation that would swoop like an eagle and besiege all their walled cities. Evangelical interpreters see this in Rome, whose standard was the eagle and whose legions besieged the cities of Judea in AD 67-70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: In the siege they will eat the flesh of their own children

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

summary: Moses foretold famine so severe in siege that even gentle mothers would eat their children. Josephus records this happening in the siege of AD 70 (it had also happened earlier, 2 Kings 6; Lamentations 4).

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Brought back to Egypt in ships and sold, with no one to buy

given.label: c. 1436 BC (Moses on the plains of Moab)

fulfilment: Josephus, Wars 6.9.2; Jerome on Jeremiah 31 / Zechariah 11
summary: Israel would be sold as slaves until no buyer was left. Josephus says captives over seventeen were sent to the Egyptian mines in AD 70. After the Bar Kokhba revolt the slave markets were so glutted that Jews sold for almost nothing.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Your cities waste, your sanctuaries desolate, your land desolate
summary: God warned that disobedience would leave the cities ruined, the sanctuaries desolate and the land empty while the people were scattered. Judea was devastated in AD 70 and again in AD 135, when Hadrian banned Jews from Jerusalem.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's seventy weeks chapter)

title: Many days without king, prince, or sacrifice
fulfilment: History: sacrifice ends with the Temple, AD 70
summary: Israel would live many days without king, prince, sacrifice or ephod, then return to the LORD and David their king in the last days. Temple sacrifice ended in AD 70 and has not resumed. The return is future.

title: Zion will be plowed like a field, Jerusalem a heap
summary: Micah warned that Zion would be ploughed like a field and the Temple hill overgrown. Jewish tradition says the Roman Turnus Rufus ploughed the Temple site, and Hadrian rebuilt the city as pagan Aelia Capitolina.

title: No survivor will remain of the house of Esau
fulfilment: Josephus, Wars 4.4-4.9; History: Idumeans vanish after AD 70
summary: Obadiah foretold that Edom would be consumed with no survivor. The Edomites (Idumeans) were absorbed into Judea under John Hyrcanus. After joining the Jewish revolt they disappeared as a people after AD 70.

sources.name: Josephus, The Wars of the Jews

title: Israel many days without king, prince or sacrifice
fulfilment: History: no Jewish king or Temple sacrifice since AD 70
summary: Hosea said Israel would live many days without a king or sacrifice and return to seek the LORD and David their king in the latter days. The first half has held since the Temple fell. The return to "David their king" is still future.

title: Jews a byword and proverb among the nations

given.label: c. 1436 BC (end of the wilderness years)

fulfilment: History: centuries of antisemitism, expulsions and pogroms
summary: Moses and Jeremiah foresaw the scattered people becoming a taunt and a byword. Expulsions from England (1290), France (1306) and Spain (1492), the pogroms and the Holocaust are usually cited as fulfilments.

title: The Jewish people preserved through the dispersion
fulfilment: History: distinct Jewish identity kept for 1,800+ years in exile
summary: God promised that although he would make a full end of the nations where Israel was scattered, he would not make a full end of Israel. They would remain a nation before him as long as the sun and moon endure. The Jews stayed a distinct people through the whole exile and the Holocaust.

title: The land left desolate while Israel is in exile
fulfilment: History: travellers' accounts of a barren, thinly settled land
summary: The land would lie desolate and enemies living there would be astonished at it. Evangelical writers point to the barren, sparsely settled land described by 19th-century visitors such as Mark Twain (1867).

title: Smyrna era: "tribulation ten days", the Roman persecutions
fulfilment: History: the persecutions from Nero to Diocletian, ended by the Edict of Milan
summary: Johnson reads the seven churches as seven church ages and starts the Smyrna age in AD 64. Many evangelicals read its "ten days" of tribulation as the ten imperial persecutions, which ended in 313.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 64 Smyrna – The Synagogue of Satan"

title: Pergamos era: church joined to state (AD 312)
fulfilment: History: Constantine's conversion and the state church
summary: Johnson dates the Pergamos age, with its stumbling block of Balaam, from AD 312. In this era he places the rise of amillennialism, cessationism and church tradition, which he sees as departures from the early teaching.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 312 Pergamos – Balaam's Stumbling Block"

title: Rome divided and the Western Empire falls (395–476)
fulfilment: History: the empire split in 395; Romulus Augustulus deposed 4 Sept 476
summary: The iron kingdom would be divided, partly strong and partly broken. Johnson's outline dates the fall of Rome to 395–476. The empire split East and West in 395, and the West fell in 476.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 395-476 Fall of Rome"
Wikipedia, Fall of the Western Roman Empire

title: Thyatira era: Jezebel and the "depths of Satan" (AD 606)
fulfilment: History: medieval church (Johnson links it with Gnosticism)
summary: Johnson starts the Thyatira age in AD 606 and links its Jezebel teaching with Gnostic-style error in the medieval church.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 606 Thyatira – Jezebel, Depths of Satan"

title: Enoch's 7th week: an apostate generation, then a sevenfold instruction
fulfilment: History (Johnson): Hillel II calendar AD 359; Karaite search c. AD 900
summary: Johnson reads Enoch's seventh week (4201–4900 AM) as the era when Jews took up Hillel II's calendar (AD 359) and Christians forgot the Zadok teaching. He links the closing "sevenfold instruction" to a search for those lost teachings around AD 900. He treats Enoch as genuine prophecy.

title: Rise of Germany (1423–1917), in Johnson's empire sequence
fulfilment: History: Holy Roman Empire / German power
summary: In Johnson's chain of empires, German power follows Papal Rome from 1423 to 1917. The verse he uses could not be read and is inferred.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1423 to 1917 Rise of Germany"

title: Sardis era: a name of life but dead ritual
summary: Johnson names Sardis "dead ritual" but no start year was visible in his contents. The date given here follows the common evangelical view that this age starts with the Reformation.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "Sardis – Dead Ritual"

title: Enoch's 8th week: a "house" for the righteous, read as the Reformation
fulfilment: History (Johnson): Protestant Reformation; Geneva Bible (1560) and King James Bible (1611)
summary: Johnson reads the eighth week's "house" as the Protestant Reformation. In its last century (AD 1576–1675) came the Geneva and King James Bibles, which drove the work of translating Scripture into every language.

title: Philadelphia era: an open door, the missionary church (1750)
fulfilment: History: the Great Awakening and the modern missions movement
summary: Johnson dates the Philadelphia "open door" age from about 1750 and calls it the missionary church. It matches the revivals and the worldwide missions movement.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1750 Philadelphia – Missionary Church"

title: Enoch's 9th week: righteous judgment revealed, read as Israel reborn
summary: Johnson takes the ninth week (5601–6300 AM) as the time the righteous judgment is shown to the world. He identifies this with Israel's rebirth in 1948, followed by the Great Tribulation and the start of the Millennium, which are still future.

title: Rise of Russia (1917–1945), in Johnson's empire sequence
summary: Johnson's empire chain ends, before modern Israel, with Russia's rise from 1917 to 1945. The verse he uses could not be read and is inferred.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1917 to 1945 Rise of Russia"

title: Fishers then hunters drive the Jews home
fulfilment: History: Zionism (the "fishers") and the persecutions and Holocaust (the "hunters")
summary: God would send fishers and then hunters to bring his people out of every hiding place. Many evangelicals read this as Zionist appeals followed by the persecutions that drove Jews toward the land.

title: Gathered out of all countries into their own land
summary: God promised to take Israel from among the nations and bring them into their own land. Evangelicals point to the modern ingathering since 1948 as the main fulfilment so far.

sources.name: Chuck Smith, Through the Bible (C2000), Ezekiel 37
Watchman Bible Study, "10 Prophecies Fulfilled in 1948" (cites Grant Jeffrey and Ken Johnson)

title: Valley of dry bones: a dead nation brought back to life
summary: Ezekiel saw dry bones come together and live: the whole house of Israel, back in its land. Chuck Smith calls it a nation dead for nineteen centuries that would live again. Coming back first and receiving the Spirit later is read as fitting a secular state now and a spiritual revival still to come.

summary: Johnson dates the last church age, lukewarm Laodicea, from 1948. It runs until the Rapture.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1948 Laodicea – Lukewarm Church"

title: The desert blossoms like the rose
summary: Isaiah saw the wilderness rejoice and blossom, with water bursting out in the desert. Evangelicals point to the reforestation and farming of the land since the late 1800s.

title: The desolate land tilled again, like the garden of Eden
fulfilment: History: resettlement and rebuilding of cities
summary: The mountains of Israel would bear fruit for the returning people, and passers-by would say the desolate land had become like Eden. Ruined cities would be rebuilt and inhabited.

title: Israel fills the face of the world with fruit
summary: Israel would blossom and bud and fill the world with fruit. Its farm exports and technology are cited. Some read the verse spiritually.

title: Planted in the land, never to be uprooted again
fulfilment: History: Israel survives every war since 1948
summary: Amos foresaw the exiles rebuilding waste cities, planting vineyards and never again being pulled up from their land. Evangelicals hold that Israel's survival of the wars since 1948 fits this.

sources.name: Watchman Bible Study, "10 Prophecies Fulfilled in 1948" (cites Grant Jeffrey and Ken Johnson)

title: Ashdod and Ashkelon resettled by Judah (from 1951)

summary: Zephaniah said the coast would belong to the remnant of Judah, who would lie down in the houses of Ashkelon. Johnson's 1951–2005 entry covers the Israeli resettlement of Ashdod and Ashkelon.

title: Jerusalem trodden down until the times of the Gentiles (7 June 1967)

summary: Jesus said Jerusalem would be trodden down by the Gentiles until the times of the Gentiles were fulfilled. Israel took the Old City on 7 June 1967. Chuck Smith saw this as the end of Gentile rule over the city. Johnson dates "Israel takes the Temple Mount" to 5892 AM, in Sivan.

Chuck Smith, Sermon Notes on Luke 21:36

title: Five cities speaking the language of Canaan (1967)

summary: Isaiah said five cities in Egypt would speak the language of Canaan. Johnson places the fulfilment in 1967. Which cities he names (probably in Sinai, then under Israeli control) could not be read.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1967 The Five Cities"

title: Judges restored as at the first: Sanhedrin re-formed (2004)
fulfilment: History: a 71-member Sanhedrin convened in Tiberias
summary: Johnson lists the re-establishment of the Sanhedrin in 2004 as a fulfilment. Rabbis convened a new 71-member Sanhedrin in Tiberias on 13 October 2004, which prophecy teachers see as preparing for a Temple. The reference here is inferred.

Wikipedia, 2004 attempt to revive the Sanhedrin

title: Many run to and fro; knowledge increases
fulfilment: History: rapid travel, science and information technology
summary: Daniel was told to seal the book until the time of the end, when many would run to and fro and knowledge would increase. Prophecy teachers point to modern travel and the information explosion. Some read it as greater understanding of prophecy itself.

title: The gospel preached in all the world before the end
fulfilment: History: modern missions and Bible translation
summary: The gospel of the kingdom would be preached to all nations as a witness, and then the end would come. Johnson ties the push to translate Scripture to the Reformation era and his Philadelphia age (1750). The work goes on, and Revelation 14:6 has an angel completing it.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "AD 1750 Philadelphia – Missionary Church"

title: A falling away and doctrines of demons in the last days

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "Unsound Doctrines of Demons"

title: Perilous times and scoffers asking "Where is his coming?"
fulfilment: History: the moral and spiritual climate of the last days
summary: The last days would bring lovers of self and money, a form of godliness without power, and scoffers who deny that Christ will return. Prophecy teachers see these traits as widespread today.

title: Birth pangs: wars, famines, earthquakes, false christs
summary: Jesus called wars, famines, pestilences, earthquakes and false messiahs the beginning of sorrows. Johnson ties the birth pangs to the time after Israel's 1948 rebirth and calls 1948 the start of the birth pangs in his Enoch reading. He also cites the Talmud's list of signs (Sanhedrin 97b).

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "The Birth Pangs"

title: Final jubilee of the Age of Grace begins (5951 AM = AD 2026)
fulfilment: Ken Johnson's Dead Sea Scroll calendar
summary: In Johnson's scheme the last 50-year jubilee of the 12th Onah starts in spring 2026 (5951 AM). He equates it with the last generation and expects revival at its start and turmoil at its end. He warns against date-setting. His Enoch page gives this jubilee as AD 2025–2075, one year off from his own conversion of 5951 AM.

sources.name: Charisma, "Is the Final Jubilee of the Age of Grace Beginning in March 2026?" (Ken Johnson interview, 30 Dec 2025)

title: Johnson's Second Coming window: 5951–6000 AM (AD 2025/26–2075)
summary: Johnson puts the Second Coming in the last century of the ninth week (5901–6000 AM, AD 1976–2075), most likely in its second jubilee (5951–6000 AM). He frames this conditionally. In an earlier book (Messianic Festivals, 2012) he put 6000 AM at roughly AD 2030–2070.

title: 120 years of warning, 1948 to 2068
summary: Johnson applies the 120-year warning before the Flood to the last days. Counting back 120 years from 2068 gives 1948, which he calls "right on time".

title: Age of Grace ends at 6000 AM (AD 2075)
summary: In Johnson's scheme the Age of Grace (Onahs 9–12, 4001–6000 AM) ends at 6000 AM, AD 2075. The Zadok priests are said to have expected the Millennium to start then. Church fathers who held the day-for-a-thousand-years view are cited for the 6,000-year pattern.

title: Micah's 4th–6th shepherds fight in Syria, reaching Nimrod's land
summary: Johnson expects three more Israeli defence ministers (and three more prime ministers) to fight on Syrian soil. One war reaches "the entrance of Nimrod's land", which he takes to be Iraq. Christ himself is the eighth leader and seventh shepherd.

sources.name: Biblefacts.org, Seven Shepherds chart (Ken Johnson ministry)
Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "4, 5, & 6 Shepherds"

title: The captives of Sepharad return to the Negev
summary: Obadiah says the exiles in Sepharad will possess the cities of the south. Johnson lists a future return of Sephardic Jews.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "Sephardic Jews Return"

title: The Rapture: believers caught up to meet the Lord
summary: The dead in Christ rise and living believers are caught up at the last trump. Johnson teaches a pre-tribulation, imminent rapture, cites early writers such as Victorinus, Cyprian and Ephraim the Syrian, and sees it pictured in the Feast of Trumpets. Chuck Smith and Skip Heitzig also teach a pre-tribulation rapture.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "The Rapture of the Church"
Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial
Connect with Skip Heitzig, interview with Thomas Ice on the pre-tribulation rapture (7 Oct 2011)

title: The false prophet and the mark of the beast (666)
summary: A second beast makes the world worship the first and forces a mark without which no one can buy or sell. Johnson cites Irenaeus on the 666 name.

title: 144,000 sealed from the tribes of Israel
summary: Twelve thousand from each tribe are sealed before the judgments. Johnson sees them winning converts in the first half of the Tribulation.

title: The seven seal judgments
summary: The seals bring conquest, war, famine and death (a quarter of the earth), martyrs, a great earthquake with the sun darkened, and silence in heaven.

title: The seven trumpet judgments
summary: The trumpets strike a third of the land, sea, waters and lights. Then come locusts for five months and an army of 200 million that kills a third of mankind. At the seventh trumpet the kingdoms become Christ's.

title: The Great Tribulation: the time of Jacob's trouble
summary: The worst distress in history falls in the last 3½ years. Johnson pictures the seven-year Tribulation in the "terrible days" between Trumpets and Yom Kippur, and expects mass martyrdom of Tribulation saints.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "The Second 3.5 Years"
Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial

title: The seven bowl judgments; the Euphrates dried up
summary: The bowls bring sores, the sea and rivers turned to blood, scorching sun and darkness. The sixth dries the Euphrates for the kings of the east, and the seventh brings the greatest earthquake and hundred-pound hail.

title: Mystery Babylon falls in one hour
summary: The harlot on the scarlet beast is judged, and the great city's plagues come in one day as merchants mourn.

title: The marriage supper of the Lamb
summary: The bride has made herself ready, and those called to the Lamb's marriage supper are blessed. The Biblefacts chart places it with the Second Coming.

title: Tribulation martyrs raised to reign with Christ
summary: Those beheaded for refusing the mark live and reign with Christ in the first resurrection. Johnson places this at the Second Coming, when the raptured saints return with Christ.

title: Judgment of the nations: sheep and goats
summary: When the Son of Man comes in glory, the nations are gathered and divided as a shepherd divides sheep from goats. Johnson places this at the Second Coming.

title: Satan bound in the abyss for a thousand years
summary: An angel binds the dragon and seals him in the bottomless pit for a thousand years, so he can deceive the nations no more until they end.

title: The Millennium: Christ reigns 1,000 years (6001–7000 AM)
summary: Christ reigns from Jerusalem for a thousand years of peace, when nations no longer learn war. Johnson's calendar starts the Kingdom age at 6001 AM (AD 2076). He sees it in the Feast of Tabernacles and cites Papias, Justin, Irenaeus and Lactantius for a literal millennium.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "The Millennial Reign"
Skip Heitzig, You Can Understand the Book of Revelation (2011), pre-tribulation premillennial

title: Ezekiel's millennial Temple and river
summary: Ezekiel sees a new Temple with a river flowing east to heal the Dead Sea, and nations go up yearly to keep Tabernacles. Dispensational teachers place this in the Millennium.

title: Israel possesses its full promised borders
summary: The land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates is divided among the twelve tribes. Johnson has a section on Israel's borders in the Millennial Reign.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (2008), contents heading "Israeli Borders"

title: The Great White Throne judgment
summary: The dead, small and great, are judged from the books, and death and Hades are thrown into the lake of fire. Johnson equates it with Enoch's "great eternal judgment" in the last part of the tenth week, 6901–7000 AM.

title: Death, sorrow and pain done away; God dwells with men
summary: God makes his dwelling with mankind and wipes away every tear. The last enemy, death, is destroyed.

title: 11Q13: Anointed one comes in the 10th jubilee (Messiah's death AD 32)
summary: 11Q13 counts history in jubilees and expects the 'anointed of the spirit' of Daniel 9:25 to appear, and the release of captives to happen, in the first week after the ninth jubilee of its age. Johnson reads this as the Messiah dying one shemitah (7 years) after the ninth jubilee ended in AD 25, which gives AD 32 (3957 AM).

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Order of Melchizedek (Goodreads quotes: ninth jubilee ends AD 25, plus one shemitah = AD 32)
dsscalendar.org Onah intro (11Q13; 3957 AM = AD 32, Nisan 14)

title: 11Q13: Atonement at the end of the 10th jubilee (end of the age, AD 75)
summary: The scroll places a final Day of Atonement for the 'lot of Melchizedek' at the end of the tenth jubilee. On Johnson's calendar that jubilee, and the 2,000-year age, closed in AD 75. It took in the atonement of AD 32 and the Temple's fall in AD 70.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, Ancient Order of Melchizedek (Goodreads quote: the end of the age was AD 75 on their calendar)

title: Herald of good news is the 'anointed of the spirit' (Isaiah 52:7)
summary: 11Q13 reads the messenger of Isaiah 52:7 as the anointed one of Daniel 9:25, who proclaims Zion's reign of God. Christians see this fulfilled in Jesus preaching the kingdom, which Johnson dates from AD 28.

title: Blind will see, lame will leap (Isaiah 35:5-6; Psalm 146:7-8)
summary: 4Q521 combines Psalm 146 and Isaiah 35 into the signs of the messianic age: captives freed, blind eyes opened, the bowed-down raised. The Gospels report Jesus healing the blind and lame as proof of who he was.

title: 4Q246: One will be called 'Son of God' and 'Son of the Most High'
summary: This Aramaic fragment uses the titles 'Son of God' and 'Son of the Most High' and is followed by an everlasting kingdom. The wording closely matches Gabriel's words to Mary in Luke 1. Scholars disagree whether the figure is the Messiah or a usurper such as Antiochus IV.

sources.name: Biblical Archaeology Review, 'An Unpublished Dead Sea Scroll Text Parallels Luke's Infancy Narrative'
Ken Johnson chronology: Messiah's birth 2 BC (Ancient Prophecies Revealed headings)

title: Son of Man's everlasting kingdom given to the saints (Daniel 7)
summary: Daniel sees one like a son of man given everlasting dominion, and the kingdom given to the saints. 4Q246 echoes this: after the 'Son of God' figure, God's people arise and their kingdom is eternal. Johnson expects the Kingdom from 6001 AM (AD 2076).

sources.name: dsscalendar.org Onah intro (first Kingdom year 6001 AM = AD 2076)

title: Shoot from the stump of Jesse, the Branch of David (Isaiah 11:1)
summary: Isaiah foretells a ruler from David's family line after it has been cut down to a stump. 4Q285 (with 11Q14) names him the 'Branch of David', who judges and leads the end-time war. Jesus was born in David's line.

title: Branch of David judges the Kittim in the final war (Isaiah 10:34)
summary: 4Q285 reads 'Lebanon will fall' as the defeat of the Kittim, the scrolls' code name for the Romans. The Branch of David strikes the wicked with the breath of his lips. Evangelicals place this at the Second Coming.

title: David's Seed: God's Son on an everlasting throne (2 Samuel 7)

fulfilled.label: 2 BC (birth of the Son of David)

summary: God promises David a son whose throne lasts forever and who will be God's son. 4Q174 says this is the 'Branch of David' who will arise in the last days together with the Interpreter of the Law. Johnson (#38) lists the near fulfilment as Solomon building the Temple (989 BC). The full fulfilment is in Jesus.

title: Rulers rage against the Lord's Anointed (Psalm 2:1-2)
summary: 4Q174 applies Psalm 2 to the last days, when the nations rise against God's Anointed and his chosen ones. The apostles said it was fulfilled when Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles and Israel joined against Jesus.

title: Fallen booth of David raised up (Amos 9:11)
summary: 4Q174 (and CD 7:16) say the fallen 'booth of David' is the Branch of David, who will rise to save Israel. James quoted Amos 9:11 to show that Gentiles coming in under Jesus fulfilled it. The national restoration is still awaited.

title: A Star out of Jacob, a Sceptre out of Israel (Numbers 24:17)
summary: 4Q175, the Damascus Document (CD 7:18-21) and the War Scroll (1QM 11:6) all read the Star and Sceptre as end-time leaders. Christians see the fulfilment in Jesus, whose birth the Magi tied to a star. Johnson separately dates the Moab and Edom part (24:17-19) to Assyria's conquests (c. 732 BC). In AD 132 Bar Kokhba ('son of the star') claimed the title and was defeated.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed (Numbers 24:17-19 applied to Moab, c. 732 BC)

title: Suffering Servant pierced for our transgressions (Isaiah 53)
summary: Isaiah describes a righteous servant who is pierced, bears others' sins, dies with the wicked and is buried with the rich. The Great Isaiah Scroll has the whole chapter in a copy made c. 125 BC (script 150–100 BC; radiocarbon 356–103 BC). That shows the text predates Jesus and was not edited to fit him.

sources.name: Josh McDowell, Evidence That Demands a Verdict (Isaiah 53 among messianic prophecies)

title: After his suffering the Servant will 'see light' (Isaiah 53:10-11)
summary: In 1QIsa-a (also 1QIsa-b and 4QIsa-d) and the Septuagint, verse 11 says that after his ordeal the Servant 'will see light'. The Masoretic text lacks this word. Evangelicals read it as the Servant living again after death, fulfilled in the resurrection.

sources.name: Isaiah Scroll (Wikipedia: 53:11 reading agrees with Septuagint)

title: Words sealed until the time of the end (Daniel 12:4)
fulfilment: Discovery and publication of the scrolls
summary: Daniel is told to seal the book until the end, when knowledge will increase. Johnson and Calvary Chapel teachers link this to the scrolls being found from 1947, and to the Temple Scroll and Damascus Document fragments coming into Israeli hands in the 1967 war, when the Temple Mount was taken. Johnson notes the Zadokite texts were mostly published only in the late 1990s.

sources.name: dsscalendar.org Enoch 7 page (scrolls found from 1948, published late 1990s)

title: War Scroll: final 40-year war of the Sons of Light against the Kittim
summary: The War Scroll lays out a final war of the Sons of Light against Belial's army and the 'Kittim'. Michael is raised up, and God wins after seven rounds of battle. Evangelicals compare it to Armageddon. Johnson expects the Tribulation to start about 2067–2068 and the Kingdom to begin by AD 2075–2076.

sources.name: dsscalendar.org Enoch 9 (Tribulation c. 2067–2068; Millennium 6000 AM = AD 2075)
Ancient Prophecies from the Dead Sea Scrolls (publisher description: end-time signs)

title: God raises up the Chaldeans (Habakkuk 1:6)
summary: Habakkuk foretold that a fierce Chaldean nation would sweep over Judah, which happened when Babylon rose to rule. The Qumran Habakkuk commentary keeps the prophecy but re-reads its 'Chaldeans' as the Kittim of its own day.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed: '607 BC Babylonian Empire' heading

title: Pesher Habakkuk: the Kittim (Romans) will overrun the land
summary: The commentary says Habakkuk's invaders are the Kittim, a code name for the Romans. They come from the coastlands, sacrifice to their standards and plunder the nations. Scholars date the commentary to 63–30 BC, so it mostly describes Rome's arrival rather than predicting it. Johnson's chronology dates Rome's rule from 64 BC.

sources.name: Pesher Habakkuk (Posen Library: date 63–30 BCE; Kittim = Romans)
Ancient Prophecies Revealed: '64 BC Rome' heading

title: Wealth of Jerusalem's last priests given to the Kittim's army
summary: The commentary predicts that the 'last priests of Jerusalem', who grew rich by plunder, will in the end have their wealth handed to the Kittim's army. This happened when Rome sacked the Temple in AD 70.

title: Though the vision tarries, wait for it (Habakkuk 2:3)
summary: 1QpHab col. 7 says the final age will last longer than the prophets said, and that God revealed the hidden timing to the Teacher of Righteousness. It tells the faithful not to slacken. Hebrews 10:37 applies the verse to Christ's return.

title: Damascus Document: root of planting 390 years after Nebuchadnezzar

fulfilled.label: c. 196 BC (+20 yrs: Teacher c. 176 BC)

summary: Ezekiel lay on his side 390 days for 390 years of Israel's sin. The Damascus Document says that 390 years after God gave Israel to Nebuchadnezzar, he caused a 'root' to sprout. They groped like the blind for 20 years, then God raised up the Teacher of Righteousness. Counting from 587/6 BC gives c. 196 BC; on Johnson's 3338 AM anchor it is 3728 AM (c. 198 BC), shortly before the c. 170 BC calendar change he describes. Johnson translated this text, but no statement of his on the 390 years was found.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The New Covenant of Damascus (translation of CD)

title: 4Q541: A priest atones for his generation yet is slandered
summary: A coming priest-figure, whose word is like heaven's, atones for all the children of his generation and drives away darkness, yet people speak lies and slander against him. Puech and others compare it with Isaiah's Suffering Servant. Johnson's Ancient Testaments of the Patriarchs presents an 'Aaron' text warning about the Messiah's first coming, which may be this scroll; this was not confirmed.

sources.name: John J. Collins, 'The Suffering Servant at Qumran', Bible Review (Dec 1993)
Ancient Mysteries of the Essenes (Aaron's warning of the First Coming)

title: 4QMMT: Moses' blessings and curses are coming true in the 'end of days'

fulfilled.label: curses to 587 BC (3338 AM); return still awaited

summary: The halakhic letter (c. 150 BC) says some of the blessings (under David and Solomon) and the curses (from Jeroboam to the exile under Zedekiah) have already come. It says the writers are living in the 'end of days', when Israel will return to the Torah. Evangelicals see the end-time return beginning in 1948.

sources.name: 4QMMT (Wikipedia: c. 150 BCE; blessings and curses in section C)
dsscalendar.org Onah intro (Temple destroyed 3338 AM, 588/7 BC)

title: Community Rule: the Prophet and the Messiahs of Aaron and Israel

fulfilled.label: AD 28–32 (prophet, priest and king in Jesus)

summary: The sect expected a prophet, a priestly Messiah from Aaron and a royal Messiah from Israel. The New Testament combines all three roles in Jesus: prophet like Moses, priest after Melchizedek, and Son of David.

title: Ruler from Bethlehem whose origins are from of old (Micah 5:2)
summary: Micah names Bethlehem as the birthplace of Israel's eternal ruler. Johnson lists it as a 'literal' prophecy fulfilled when Jesus was born there. The Minor Prophets scroll from Wadi Murabba'at preserves Micah in a text close to the Masoretic.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed, Introduction (Micah 5:2, literal prophecy)

title: 69 weeks from the decree to Messiah the Prince (Daniel 9:25-26)

given.label: c. 536 BC (1st year of Darius the Mede)

summary: Johnson counts 483 prophetic years of 360 days from Artaxerxes' decree in March 444 BC, which lands on 6 April AD 32, with Messiah 'cut off' days later. 11Q13 cites Daniel 9:25's 'anointed one'. Daniel 9 is preserved at Qumran in 4Q116 (9:12-17), but verses 24-27 do not survive there.

sources.name: Ken Johnson, The Rapture (Daniel's 70 weeks; April 6, AD 32)
Daniel 11 Time Map (biblefacts.org: Darius the Mede 536–530 BC)

title: Statue of four kingdoms, ending with Rome (Daniel 2)

fulfilled.label: 64 BC (Rome, the iron kingdom); stone kingdom future

fulfilment: History of Babylon, Persia (537 BC), Greece (326 BC), Rome (64 BC)
summary: Nebuchadnezzar's dream statue stands for Babylon, Medo-Persia, Greece and Rome. A stone not cut by hands then crushes it. Johnson's dates for the empires are 607, 537, 326 and 64 BC. The kingdom of God is still to come. Daniel 2 survives at Qumran in 4QDan-a.

sources.name: Ancient Prophecies Revealed: headings 607 BC Babylon, 537 BC Cyrus, 326 BC Alexander, 64 BC Rome

title: Goat with a great horn conquers the ram (Daniel 8:5-8, 21)
fulfilment: Alexander the Great's conquest of Persia
summary: The goat from the west, named as Greece, shatters the Medo-Persian ram. Its great horn is broken and four horns arise. This matches Alexander and the four kingdoms that followed him. Qumran copies of Daniel 8 (4QDan-a, -b) show the text was already circulating in the 2nd century BC.

title: King of the North profanes the sanctuary (Daniel 11:31)

fulfilled.label: 165 BC (Johnson's map; desecration Dec 167 BC secular)

summary: Daniel describes a northern king who stops the daily sacrifice and sets up the abomination of desolation, which matches Antiochus IV Epiphanes. A 2025 radiocarbon and AI script study dated 4Q114 (4QDan-c, which has Daniel 10-11) to c. 230–160 BC. That challenges the theory that Daniel was written after 164 BC. Jesus said this foreshadows the future Antichrist.

sources.name: Daniel 11 Time Map (biblefacts.org: Antiochus IV 175–164 BC; typifies Antichrist 165 BC)
Associates for Biblical Research, 'Dead Sea Scroll 4Q114 and the Date of Daniel' (Popović et al. 2025)
Ancient Prophecies Revealed, Introduction (Daniel 11 typological prophecy)

title: Enoch's 5th week: the house of glory built (1 Enoch 93:7)
summary: In the Apocalypse of Weeks, Enoch sees a house of glory built at the end of the fifth week. Johnson identifies it as Solomon's Temple, dedicated in 2935 AM, within week 5 (2801–3500 AM). Aramaic copies of the Apocalypse of Weeks survive in 4QEn-g.

title: Enoch's 6th week: a man ascends (1 Enoch 93:8)
summary: In the sixth week everyone is blinded, a man ascends, and the house of dominion is burned. Johnson places the week in 3501–4200 AM (425 BC–AD 275). He takes the man who ascends to be Jesus, whose ascension he dates to 3957 AM (AD 32).

title: Enoch's 6th week: the house of dominion burned with fire
summary: The same week sees the house burned and the chosen root scattered. Johnson dates the burning of Herod's Temple by Rome to 3995 AM (AD 70) and the Roman dispersion after Bar Kokhba to 4057 AM (AD 132).

title: Enoch's 6th week: the chosen root dispersed (AD 132)
fulfilment: Bar Kokhba revolt and Roman expulsion
summary: Johnson identifies the scattering of the 'chosen root' with Rome driving Israel out after the Bar Kokhba revolt. He dates it to 4057 AM (AD 132), the start of a dispersion that lasted until 1948.

title: Enoch's 7th week: an apostate generation, then sevenfold wisdom
fulfilment: Hillel II calendar (AD 359); Karaite movement (c. AD 900)
summary: Enoch foresees an apostate generation in week 7, at whose end the elect receive sevenfold instruction. Johnson points to the AD 359 Hillel II calendar replacing the Zadokite one. He sees a partial recovery of lost teaching around AD 900, when the Karaites were said to have found scrolls in the Judean hills.

title: Enoch's 8th week: righteousness, and a house built for the Great King
summary: The eighth week, one of righteousness, is given a sword against oppressors, and a house is built for the Great King. Johnson applies this to the Reformation: churches cleared of idols, and the Geneva and King James Bibles spreading Scripture, with completion in 5501–5600 AM (AD 1576–1675).

title: Enoch's 9th week: righteous judgment revealed (Israel 1948)
summary: In week 9 (AD 1676–2375 on Johnson's count) righteous judgment is revealed to the whole world and the world is marked for destruction. Johnson takes the rebirth of Israel in 5873 AM (1948) as the opening sign, 120 years before his proposed Tribulation start (c. 2068).

title: Enoch's 9th week: world written down for destruction, then Millennium
summary: Johnson reads the rest of week 9 as the seven-year Tribulation, possibly starting about March 2067–2068, followed by the Messiah's thousand-year reign from 6000/6001 AM (AD 2075–2076), which the Zadok priests are said to have expected.
